title: Non-monotonic "ratchet" naming: setRatio freely re-sets ratio up or down within [0, MAX_RATIO]
description: The "Ratchet" name (NudgeRatchet / NudgeRatchetMintDebtHook) implies a monotonic, one-directional (up-only) mechanism, but setRatio (line 80) freely re-sets the ratio to any value in [0, MAX_RATIO], up or down, with no monotonicity constraint. This is a cosmetic Law-2 spec/naming deviation: the implementation is internally consistent and safe, but the name advertises a monotonic invariant the code does not enforce. Recorded under the same story-035 faithfulness tag (F-02-035) as the naming aspect of the decimal-scale finding.
impact: Cosmetic / spec-conformance only. No asset, value, or availability impact. Risk is reader/operator confusion: someone relying on the "ratchet" name to assume the ratio can only increase would be mistaken.
attackPath: Owner calls setRatio with a value lower than the current ratio.
setRatio accepts it (only bound is [0, MAX_RATIO]); no monotonic-up check.
The 'ratchet' invariant implied by the name is violated, though no unsafe state results.
recommendation: Either enforce monotonic-up semantics in setRatio (require new >= current) to match the 'ratchet' name, or rename the component / document that the ratio is freely settable in both directions so the name does not over-promise a monotonic invariant.
